title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine was one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It halts: busycoq pull request 105 proves it in Rocq (compiled here). This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 105 (Alex Havrilla of DeepMind, 2026-11-19) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open.

What this repository found on its own (background). The head sweeps over the period-6 word 111110, which appears in all six rotations, and the leftward sweep over each rotation is a proved shift rule. Five or six walls between rotations split the tape into domains; between consecutive visits of the right end the domain lengths change by amounts in ratio 4 and the width grows by 1024. This looks like a counter in base 4; its rule was not written here. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 99,661 cells have been visited and 67,922 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.19×10<sup>18</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 7,191,166,652,716,873,648 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,036,035 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.27×10<sup>145</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran with blocks of 6 cells, from blank tape for 1202 seconds and reached step 2.27×10145 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 25 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The leftward sweep over the background in the four rotations it is entered in: L (111110)^n E>1 R, L (111101)^n A>1 R, L (101111)^n D>1 R and L (011111)^n C>1 R, each copy becoming a rotation of 101011, for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Domains changing in ratio 4
claims.text: The right end is visited rarely (325 times in 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps). Between consecutive visits late in the run the width grows by 1024, the first domain by 1536, and the other domains change by −384, −96, −24, −6 (each a quarter of the one before). Domain lengths are often powers of 2 or sums of few (4096, 1792, 448, 256, 872). Read off the run; not proved.

claims.title: Halting, in this repository's own proofs
claims.text: Decided outside: busycoq pull request 105 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here, no axioms; see above), at hub 1,211,452, far beyond any run made here (no halt in 7.19·10<sup>18</sup> steps). Not proved by this repository's own Lean, which has the sweep rules only.

explainer.lede: It halts, after far more than 1080 steps. The tape is the six cells 111110 repeated, in stretches (domains) separated by short walls; at each visit of the head to the right end the domains nearest it shrink by fixed amounts, like the digits of a counter counting down. Busycoq pull request 105 follows this for 1,211,452 visits until the first domain runs out and the machine stops.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 99,661 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Ratio of the changes of consecutive domains between visits of the right end.

sections.heading: Exact counting for 11,120 visits, then a countdown with a reserve
html: The proof is busycoq pull request 105 by Alex Havrilla of DeepMind: a Rocq file of 4,044 lines. It was compiled here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch, in 13 seconds, and it uses no axioms (recorded in holdouts/external.json). Its main theorem is halt : halts tm c0: from the blank tape, the machine halts.

The shape. Write wn for the word w written n times. The proof writes the tape as a list of numbers, each number a standing for the word 0 1a+1. A 4 is 011111, one period of the background, and a 2 is 0111, a wall. It watches the machine at hubs: the head in state B on the blank cell right of everything. At a hub the tape is a short prefix next to the head, then a domain of b0 copies of 011111, a wall, a domain of b1 copies, a wall, and so on. The state is a prefix (one of four) and the list of domain lengths b0, b1, ...

Stage 1: exact. A step function on this list, proved to match the machine, carries the blank tape through the first 11,120 hubs, about 1.49·1033 machine steps. The computer runs it with binary numbers (vm_compute) in 15 checked pieces. At hub 11,120 the prefix is 0 5 5 and the domains are 156,691, then 3,931,792, then 19,317,108, then 14 more up to 1.24·1016.

Stage 2: the countdown. From there each sweep costs more than 1027 steps, so the proof switches to lemmas that hold for every value. One cycle of 3 hubs (cycle_3_step) takes 9 from the first domain and 28 from the second. It also changes the third domain and everything beyond it, in ways the proof does not compute. Instead it bounds them with a potential W, a weight summed over the deeper part of the tape. The lemma mCL_bump_spec, proved by strong induction, says the third domain never loses more than 117 per cycle beyond what W pays for. So the far part acts as a reserve that never runs dry, and the cycle can be repeated. After 17,410 cycles the first domain is down to 1. Two transition hubs follow, and the prefix becomes 0 3. The old second domain, now 3,444,302 long, comes first. A cycle of 3 hubs then takes 9 from it each time (cycle_2_step), and after 382,700 cycles 2 are left.

The halt. With 2 copies left, the lemma hub_03_halt runs a few more sweeps. They end with the head in state E on a 0 at the right end, with nothing to its right. E then writes a 1 and moves right into state F on a 0, and F0 is the halting transition. That is hub 1,211,452, after far more than 1080 steps. At that point the reserve still has about 4.65 million to spare.

Computer and algebra. The computer checks stage 1, the 11,120 exact hubs. Ordinary proofs, valid for every value, handle the base transitions, the potential and its bound, the two cycles and their repetition by induction, and the halt. The ratio-4 pattern seen on this page is most likely this counter seen at other moments. The proof never needs its exact rule, because the deeper digits only have to stay large.

sections.heading: One word in six rotations
html: The tape repeats 111110, but in different rotations in different domains; the walls between domains are phase shifts. The leftward sweeps are proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean). Two end turns at step 3.7·108:

sections.heading: Changes in ratio 4
html: The head reaches the right end rarely (325 times in the first 2·109 steps). Between two such visits late in the run the width grows by 1024 cells, the first domain grows by 1536, and the next domains change by −384, −96, −24, −6: each change a quarter of the one before. With domain lengths like 4096 and 1792 that suggests a counter in base 4 whose digits are the domains. The rule has not been extracted.

sections.heading: Two 0s
html: F0 is the only halting transition, reached as E>0 0. The background never has two 0s in a row; the ends of the tape do (1100 at the right end above), so the question was whether the counter ever brings E there in the wrong phase. It does: the proof of pull request 105 (first section) brings E onto the right end on a 0 with nothing beyond it, at hub 1,211,452.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).
After 109 steps the tape spans 99,661 cells (69,823 left of the start, 105 right), with a density of 1s of 0.682.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer over the period-6 background 111110 in all its rotations; five or six walls (phase shifts) split it into domains whose lengths change between visits of the right end by amounts in ratio 4 (−384, −96, −24, −6), with powers of 2 throughout: a counter-like structure not yet written as a rule. Decided outside: busycoq PR 105 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here).
family: period-6 bouncer with walls, ratio-4 hierarchy
